newsitem.title: USA: Calif. official orders auto insurers to cut rates.
newsitem.headline: Calif. official orders auto insurers to cut rates.

text.p: California Insurance Commissioner Chuck Quackenbush on Thursday ordered insurers selling automobile policies to reduce their rates to reflect the expected savings from a November ballot measure.
Quackenbush issued a "bulletin" that requires the insurers to include in their rate filings projected savings from Proposition 213. The filings are due by February 18.

Proposition 213, approved on November 5 by a 77 to 13 percent margin, prohibits uninsured motorists and convicted drunk drivers from collecting pain and suffering damages for injuries sustained in an accident.

It also prevents felons from collecting any damages for injuries they might sustain while committing a crime or fleeing from a crime scene. The measure applies to personal injury claims with trial dates after January 1, 1997.
An insurance department study estimated that companies would pay out $327 million less in claims annually under the measure.

"Three out of four voters supported Prop. 213 because they believe in personal responsibility and because this measure is a fair and sensible way to reduce auto insurance rates," Quackenbush said. "Insurers must keep their part of the bargain and pass on projected savings to their customers."
